facts.liveHelp:
Watching the match
The half you are watching has already been played by the game. You are seeing it back minute by minute.
Every goal, shot, save, corner, throw in, foul and card is the real one, at its real minute. The passing and running in between is drawn to fit them.
The score changes when the ball is in the net, not before.
A goal marked (P) was a penalty. A goal marked (O.G) is an own goal: it counts for the club it is listed under, and the man named put it into his own net.
Tap one of your players to make a sub or change shape. Everything up to that minute stays. The rest of the half is played again with your change.
Pause, pick a speed, or Skip to the whistle. Tap a goal card to move on.

Worked example: It is 0-0 at 61'. You tap your striker, bring on fresh legs and go Attacking. The first 61 minutes stay exactly as they were. From 62' the half is played again with your change, and that new half is what you watch next.

facts.entry: Club Manager: (P) and (O.G) beside a goal, and Quick Sim uses the bench. You asked for all three. In Club Manager a penalty now reads (P) after the scorer everywhere a goal is listed: the full time report, the match timeline and the live match. And now and then a goal is an own goal, marked (O.G) under the club that got it, with the defender or keeper who put it into his own net. It is always one of the goals the match already had, so no score, result or table moves. The player who would have had it loses it from his season, nobody else gains it, and an own goal has no assist. A penalty is never an own goal, and a shootout kick is not a goal, so it gets no mark. And when you Quick Sim, the coach now makes changes after the break too, not only for injuries: around the hour and again in the run in he takes off a booked man or the most tired legs for a fresher player who plays there, as long as the side is no weaker for it, or whatever it costs once you are two goals clear. He keeps one change back for an injury, and the full time report lists every sub he made. Coming on counts for what it is, too: in a player's last ten a start is a game and a sub gets the share of the match he played, so ten minutes at the end does not keep a star man you dropped quiet, and the squad screens now show starts and matches off the bench.
